label: trigger token w/d/0/z/c mid-input, after a sequence opening with g/h/i/j/k/n/r/v/y/e
explanation: Fires only in the original-input phase, almost entirely at t=3..7 (none at t<2, the delimiter, or the copy phase). Requires the current input to be a trigger token: w (36% of mass), d (26%), 0 (17%), z (9%), c (8%), with a weak tail on f. The top activations are all w or d. Whether a trigger fires depends on the earlier context, mostly the first two original tokens. Openings with j, y, v, g, h, k, r, n, i, e make it likely (about 50-85% precision). Openings with c, d, f, o, p, q, w, z or the digits 0/2/3 suppress it almost completely. Later tokens seem to have a similar but weaker graded effect, so the hidden-state context acts like a weighted sum, which the predicate only approximates. It mostly fires on the first occurrence of the token (91% of mass). Dev: P=0.47, R=0.77, mass recall 0.86. It does not fire on triggers at t<=2, or on non-trigger tokens whatever the context.
